foundation.introP1: The foundational pieces a company needs before large specs and major engineering work: who we are, what we build, how people and systems are organized.
foundation.introP2: Each foundation item has its own page: what it is, why it matters, when it appears, how to build it, and how to know it is done.
howToRead: 3. Decision rights — who approves scope, timeline, budget, and risk.
4. Product and goals — why work is taken on.
5. Intake and prioritization — how requests enter the process.
6. System map and glossary — landscape and domain language.
7. Data ownership — owners of layers, models, and access.
8. Engineering baseline and legal/vendors — quality and data constraints.
9. Implementation plan — initiative order and dependencies.
10. Business processes — lanes, handoffs, and gates.
11. Then — task framing and detailed specifications.
foundation.orgNextHint: Org structure sets the role skeleton. The next required step is job descriptions: what each role does, what authority it has, and which outcomes it owns.
foundation.intakeToProcessText: Reject / Park / Discovery. If the decision is Discovery, task-process stage 1 starts next (not “straight into engineering”).
foundation.jobDescriptionsDiagramNote: Org structure answers “which teams and roles exist”. Job descriptions answer “what exactly a person in this role must do and what authority they have”.
foundation.jdExampleCardText: A full Mid Frontend Engineer job description: mission, outcomes, decision rights, out of scope, collaboration, success criteria, leveling ladder, and process participation.
foundation.jdExampleDialogHint: A teaching sample JD in the style of large product companies. Not an HR sheet that says “helps the team”, but a working expectations contract.

hints.componentsIntro: Current platform and new boundary. Detailed breakdown of each service — in the full spec.
hints.workSequenceIntro: End-to-end happy path: from launch to saving in reports.
hints.dataContractsIntro: Illustrative JSON at concept (not final OpenAPI yet). Formal paths and schemas — in the full spec.
hints.storageEntitiesIntro: Which entities will appear — not migrations yet, but enough to estimate.
hints.prerequisitesIntro: Data and API work without which the module cannot launch honestly.
hints.modelOutputToUiIntro: Semantic brief for design before mockups: which model fields live on the map, panel, and report.
hints.dataReadinessIntro: What the risk/loss model needs vs what the platform already has. Before concept and design we lock prerequisite work.
hints.discoverySquadIntro: Staffed after problem framing — by problem type. This is the entry into research, not the delivery team roster.
hints.processTouchpointsIntro: During research we capture which existing processes the feature will touch. Full to-be diagrams and rules come at concept.
hints.userFlowIntro: Main happy path. Below — full business process with limits, failures, and notifications.
hints.businessProcessIntro: Rules the designer already reflects in the prototype. Formal APIs and schemas — in architecture and full spec.
hints.platformIntegrationsIntro: How one feature plugs into existing processes: billing, notifications, reports, map.
hints.operationalReadinessIntro: Before release: not QA alone. Monitoring, flags, rollback, migrations — green tests are not the same as production readiness.
hints.modelIoIntro: Semantic examples (not final OpenAPI yet). Designer and architect look at the same fields.
hints.platformSliceIntro: What's already on the platform, what's missing, and what blocks our MVP — with workarounds so we don't wait for everything.
hints.ganttOrder: Order: first model and pipeline, then UI + backend. In parallel — data/layers and billing (only credit debit → soft-limit).
hints.apiContractsIntro: Formal endpoints for engineering and QA. Request/response examples.
